cohort: 300 women undergoing obstetric surgery were enrolled from Sree Balaji Medical College and Hospital, Chennai, India.
finding: The overall incidence of surgical site infections (SSIs) was 6.7%, with significant risk factors including age 30-40 years, obesity, diabetes mellitus, preoperative vaginal discharge, multiple vaginal examinations (>5), prolonged hospital stay (>14 days), and use of interrupted sutures.
mod_finding: Infection rates were higher in emergency obstetric surgeries (7.2%) compared to elective procedures (5.1%).
